record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.context_brief: Branch-width of excluded minors for real representability
record.original_question: Is there a uniform integer n such that every excluded minor for the class of real-representable matroids has branch-width at most n?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Is there an integer n such that all excluded minors for the class of R-representable matroids have branch-width ≤ n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A matroid M is real-representable if there exist a positive integer r and vectors assigned to the ground set of M, taking values in some vector space over the field of real numbers R, such that the rank function of M coincides with the linear-algebraic rank function of the assigned vectors. The class of real-representable matroids is closed under taking minors (deletion and contraction of elements), and an excluded minor for this class is a matroid M that is not real-representable but such that every proper minor of M is real-representable.

The branch-width of a matroid M with ground set E is defined as follows. A branch-decomposition of M is a pair (T, μ) where T is a tree in which every internal vertex has degree 3 and μ is a bijection between E and the set of leaves of T. Each edge e of T partitions the leaves of T into two sets, inducing a partition (A, E \ A) of E; the width of e is r_M(A) + r_M(E \ A) - r(M) + 1, where r_M denotes the rank function of M. The width of the branch-decomposition is the maximum width of an edge of T, and the branch-width of M is the minimum width of a branch-decomposition of M (with the convention used for matroids of small size). 

Question: Does there exist an integer n such that every excluded minor for the class of real-representable matroids has branch-width at most n?
artifact.category_tag: Matroid theory: excluded minors and branch-width
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Searches turn up the original problem list and related work on excluded minors and branch-width (e.g., results by Geelen-Gerards-Whittle bounding branch-width of excluded minors over finite fields), but no resolution for the real-representable case. Real-representable matroids are known to have infinitely many excluded minors, and no uniform bound on their branch-width has been established.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 4.1. Is there an integer n such that all excluded minors for the class of R-representable matroids have branch-width ≤ n?
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the excluded minors for the matroids of branch-width k
status_evidence.snippet: Excluded minors for matroids of branch-width k have size at most (6^k - 1)/5; for each finite field GF(q) and each k, only finitely many GF(q)-representable matroids are excluded minors of branch-width ≤ k.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds are known over finite fields, but no analogous bound is established for R-representable matroids.
